title: IPL auction returns to India with Lucknow holding the biggest purse
excerpt: The IPL 2027 mini-auction will be held in Goa on 16 December, the first in India for three years, with 66 squad places to fill.
content_html:
The Indian Premier League's player auction will return to India for the first time in three years when franchises gather at ITC Grand Goa on 16 December.

The BCCI confirmed the venue after franchises raised concerns about the logistics of staging the event overseas. The past three auctions were held in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi.

A mini-auction to finish the cycle

This is a mini-auction, so teams are topping up squads rather than rebuilding them. It is also the last mini-auction of the 2023-27 cycle, before the next full mega-auction.

The ten franchises have retained 184 players, 55 of them from overseas. That leaves 66 places to fill, including 25 overseas spots.

Who has the most to spend

  • Lucknow Super Giants: ₹47.45 crore, the largest purse, with seven places to fill
  • Sunrisers Hyderabad: ₹40.15 crore and seven places
  • Delhi Capitals: ₹39.5 crore
  • Mumbai Indians: ₹32.6 crore

Sunrisers have more room after releasing Australian opener Travis Head, who has chosen to skip the 2027 season.

Names in the pool

The release lists include several proven players. Among them are New Zealand left-armer Trent Boult, West Indian batter Shimron Hetmyer, and Indian players Deepak Chahar, Avesh Khan and Nitish Rana. Delhi released Australian quick Mitchell Starc, though it is not yet known whether he will enter the auction.

Players have to register to be included, so the final list could still change.

The women's league is already set

The Women's Premier League held its own 2027 auction in Kochi on 28 October. The WPL season runs from 14 January to 7 February 2027, so its squads will be in action weeks before the men's competition begins.

A clash on the day

The auction falls on the same day as India's second one-day international against Sri Lanka in Bengaluru.

Goa is four and a half hours behind AEST, so an afternoon session in India will run into the evening for viewers on Australia's east coast.

Chennai Super Kings will be bidding without MS Dhoni for the first time. The former captain retired as a player on 17 November and will mentor the side.
